title: Mixtures and how to separate them
examples: If I have muddy water, what can I use to clean it?
How can I get pure salt from seawater?
Can you show me how to separate ink colors?

explain.say: Today we learn how to separate mixtures into pure parts.

draw.text: Mixtures and how to separate them

items: We use methods to separate them.
The method depends on the substances.

explain.say: Filtering uses a filter to separate solids from liquids.
Evaporation leaves solid residue when a liquid turns to gas.
Distillation separates liquids with different boiling points.
Chromatography separates coloured components by how fast they travel.
When you get salt from seawater, you use evaporation followed by crystallization.

faq.q: What is the difference between evaporation and distillation?
faq.a: Evaporation leaves a solid behind, like salt. Distillation collects the liquid as it turns to gas and then cools.
asks: How do I get pure water?

faq.q: Can filtering separate salt from water?
faq.a: No, filtering only catches large solid pieces. Salt dissolves and passes right through the filter paper.
It separates different coloured dyes or pigments in a mixture. The different colours travel at different speeds up the paper.
asks: Is it about colour or size?

faq.q: Do I need heat for all these methods?
faq.a: No, filtering and chromatography do not require heat. Evaporation and distillation do require heat energy.

faq.q: What is the stationary phase in chromatography?
faq.a: The stationary phase is the material that stays put, like the paper or cardboard strip. The moving liquid carries the mixture along it.
asks: What stays still in the process?

facts: Filtering separates insoluble solids from liquids.
Evaporation is used to recover dissolved solids from a liquid.
Distillation is used to separate liquids based on boiling points.
Chromatography separates mixtures of coloured substances.

quiz.say: To get pure water from salt water, which process is best?
quiz.why: Distillation boils the water into steam and then cools it back to liquid form, leaving the salt behind.

wrong.0: Filtering will not remove the dissolved salt particles from the water.
wrong.1: Evaporation leaves the salt behind, and the water vapour escapes and is lost.
wrong.2: Chromatography separates colours, not dissolved salts from water.

quiz.say: If you mix black ink and run it through chromatography, what do you observe?

options.show: The ink remains one solid black spot.
options.say: The ink remains one solid black spot.

quiz.why: Different coloured dyes in the ink have different chemical properties, causing them to travel up the paper at different speeds.

wrong.0: This assumes all colours travel at the same speed, which is not true for inks.
wrong.1: The process only separates the components; it does not stain the paper itself.
wrong.2: Chromatography relies on the interaction between the ink and the paper to cause movement.

quiz.say: Which method uses a barrier to catch large, undissolved particles?
quiz.why: A filter material acts as a barrier, allowing only the liquid to pass through while trapping the solid matter.

wrong.0: Distillation separates liquids based on their boiling points, not solid matter.
wrong.1: Chromatography separates colours in a liquid, not large suspended solids.
wrong.3: Evaporation separates dissolved solids, not large solid particles.
